lecture_summary.lecture_name: Kinetics of Particles and Rigid Body Dynamics – Equations of Motion, Tension & Inertia
lecture_summary.summary: This lecture discusses the kinetics of particles, introduces Newton's Second Law, force and kinetic diagrams, and applies these to particles and rigid bodies. It includes worked problems on pendulum and conical motion (tension in cord, reaction forces), derivations of the equations of motion for rigid bodies, and the concept of moment of inertia.

key_takeaways.section_title: Newton's Second Law for Particles and Rigid Bodies
key_takeaways.description: Newton's Second Law governs particle motion as \( \vec{F} = m\vec{a} \), and for a system of particles or a rigid body, summing over all constituent particles leads to force and moment equations.
Free-body diagrams (FBD) and kinetic diagrams represent force and acceleration relationships. They are key in mechanically analyzing and solving problems for both particles and rigid bodies.
The moment of inertia \( I \) is defined as \( I = \int r^2 \; dm \). Parallel axis theorem is \( I_P = I_G + md^2 \).

learning_objectives.section_title: Apply Newton’s Second Law to Particles
learning_objectives.description: Students should be able to write and use \( \vec{F} = m\vec{a} \) for single particles and solve for unknowns using FBD and kinetic diagrams.

learning_objectives.section_title: Extend Newton’s Laws to Rigid Bodies
learning_objectives.description: Understand how force and moment summations lead to the equations \( \sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}_G \), \( \sum \vec{M}_G = I_G \alpha \).

learning_objectives.section_title: Analyze Planar Motion of Rigid Bodies
learning_objectives.description: Write and utilize planar equations of motion for translation and rotation, including use of the center of mass location.

technical_concepts.description: Used for both particles (\( \sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a} \)) and rigid bodies (\( \sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}_G \), \( \sum \vec{M}_G = I_G \alpha \)).
In curved motion, accelerations have tangential (\( a_t \)) and normal (\( a_n \)) components: \( a_t = \dot{v} \), \( a_n = v^2/r \).

technical_concepts.section_title: Moment of Inertia and Parallel Axis Theorem
technical_concepts.description: \( I = \int r^2 dm \); \( I_P = I_G + md^2 \). The radius of gyration is \( k = \sqrt{I/m} \).
